llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (local browser-extension collection + Feishu export) is plausible and some pieces line up, but there are multiple incoherencies and risky options (developer-default paths, mismatched script paths, remote-SSH execution, and arbitrary bridge startup commands) that make it unclear whether the bundle is safe to run as-is.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (browser-extension + local bridge collection) match the included scripts and required binaries (curl, node). However there are inconsistencies: SKILL.md and examples use {baseDir}/scripts/*.sh while run.sh invokes bridge/collect_and_export_loop.sh (different path). run.sh also hardcodes a developer local default WORKDIR (/Users/zhym/...), which is not appropriate for general consumers and suggests the package expects a different repository layout. These mismatches mean the provided scripts may not run correctly unless the user reparents files or has the original repo layout.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to start local bridge servers, call localhost API endpoints, and export via Feishu (handled by the extension). The scripts can: start an arbitrary BRIDGE_CMD (nohup of any command), run node -e JavaScript, and—via run.sh—invoke SSH to a remote host and run the collect script there. Those capabilities are expected for a collector but grant broad ability to execute arbitrary commands locally or remotely if the bridge command or remote host is controlled by an attacker or misconfigured. SKILL.md also references optional env vars (WEB_COLLECTION_*) not listed in requires.env, and the README explicitly instructs to run the bundled scripts first (prescriptive but okay).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with bundled shell scripts; there is no external installer or downloaded archive. That keeps installation risk low compared to remote downloads or package installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, which is consistent with being runnable locally. But the code relies on optional env vars (WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL, WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH, WEB_COLLECTION_LOCAL_WORKDIR, etc.) and allows passing a BRIDGE_CMD that could run arbitrary processes. Remote operation requires SSH access to a collector host (implicit credential requirement) but the skill does not declare or document that credential need explicitly. The implicit need for SSH keys/credentials and use of arbitrary bridge commands is disproportionate if a user expects a purely local, read-only collector.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or global agent config. It runs as-needed scripts and has no installer that claims persistent system integration. Remote SSH execution is available but controlled by the REMOTE_SSH variable supplied by the user.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the described data-collection loop, but several things don’t add up and you should verify before running: 1) File layout mismatch: SKILL.md/examples refer to scripts/..., while run.sh expects a bridge/ directory and a specific WORKDIR (a developer’s home path). Make sure the paths match your checkout and that you understand where code will run. 2) BRIDGE_CMD is an arbitrary command the script will nohup and run as your user — don’t pass a bridge-cmd you don’t trust. 3) Remote mode uses SSH to run the collector on a remote host: only use REMOTE_SSH if you control the remote machine and its keys; otherwise stick to local mode. 4) The Feishu export is handled by the browser extension; verify the extension’s permissions and configuration (and examine the actual bridge/extension code) before exporting sensitive data. 5) Prefer running these scripts in an isolated environment (container or dedicated VM) and inspect the bridge server and extension source code if available. If you need help mapping the repository layout or removing developer-default paths, get that fixed before executing any commands.
